descriptionChirho: The noun yothereth (יֹתֶרֶת) meaning 'lobe, appendage' — specifically the caudate lobe or fatty appendage of the liver, prescribed to be burned on the altar in Levitical sacrificial instructions (Exod 29:13,22; Lev 3:4,10,15; 4:9; 7:4; 8:16,25; 9:10,19). English renders as appendage/lobe; Spanish lóbulo 'lobe'; Hindi जिगर के ऊपर की झिल्ली (membrane over the liver) and लपेट 'covering/wrapping'; Arabic الزِّيَادَة (az-ziyada) 'the excess/appendage'; Korean 덮개 (deopgae) 'cover' and 간 위의 꼬리 (tail on the liver); Swahili kitambi/utando 'small lobe/membrane.' Both clusters describe the identical anatomical structure — one uses the construct form with article (the appendage of...) and the other the absolute form (the lobe). All 11 occurrences are the same sacrificial-anatomical term.
